segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Orthic Triangle H a H b H c and the Tangential Triangle T A T B T C form a classic dual pair. The orthic triangle is both the cevian and pedal triangle of the Orthocenter X four, while the tangential triangle is bounded by the tangents to the circumcircle at A, B, and C, with perspector at the Symmedian Point X six.

segments.text: Because the circumcircle radius to each vertex A, B, C is perpendicular to the corresponding side of the orthic triangle, the sides of the orthic triangle and the sides of the tangential triangle are strictly parallel! Consequently, the orthic and tangential triangles are homothetic.

segments.text: In acute triangles, the Orthocenter X four is the incenter of the orthic triangle, while the radical axis and cross-intersections of the orthic and reference triangles produce the Clawson Point X nineteen.
